why: For a day i, the nearest lower day is either the previous strictly smaller element or the next strictly smaller element, whichever is closer. Two monotonic-stack passes compute both for all days in O(n), and each query is then O(1).
hints: The nearest lower day on the left and the nearest lower day on the right are independent questions. Which classic stack query answers each?
Previous smaller element (scan left to right) and next smaller element (scan right to left), each with a stack that pops while the top is >= the current price.
Precompute prev[] and nxt[] in O(n), then for each query compare distances i - prev and nxt - i, preferring prev on ties (smaller day number), and convert to 1-based. O(n + q).
pitfalls: Ties in distance go to the earlier day (the left candidate).
Days are 1-based in both queries and answers.
Strictly lower: equal prices do not count, so pop on >=.
Answering each query by scanning outwards is O(n) per query, too slow for 10^5 queries.
